propositions: Detached compaction sweep that dies between snapshot write/retire and git commit leaves the tracker tree dirty with tracked deletions and untracked snapshot files, blocking the next reconverge union merge and stranding local commits.

A crash-atomic fold implementation using intent journal (written before mutation), ordered mutation with try/except rollback, and startup recovery that discriminates landed vs. abandoned folds eliminates the dirty-tree wedge.

Recovery must never delete folded-event bytes: incomplete rollback retains the uncommitted snapshot as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT for fsck repair, and recovery discrimination preserves events in all paths (reverted, superseded, or fsck-retained).

Transient git faults during recovery probes (timeouts, index.lock contention) must be distinguished from snapshot-absent to prevent misclassification of a transient failure as a landed or superseded fold, which would incorrectly revert or discard data.
